bio: Don't be fooled by the nondescript exterior, as this lively and friendly place welcomes guests with an appealing rustic and authentic Mexican ambience. Stop in the lounge at the entrance for a drink before heading to your table, though if you enjoy being in the center of it all while watching the team cook over a wood-fired grill, then there's no better spot than a seat at the horseshoe counter. The menu is tightly edited, featuring a handful of dishes ranging from small plates and masas to meatier entrees. Everything is vibrant, full of flavor, and designed for sharing, so order with abandon to sample it all. Their list of tequila and mezcal is impressive, and the helpful staff is always on hand to offer recommendations....
